request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The steward's dashboard counts are now over the sheet and all its descendants.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The steward's dashboard now counts pending, review and overdue claims across the sheet and all its descendants. All 4 tests in the spec pass under `bin/e2e`.

**The change:**
- `src/main/frontend/features/dashboard/dashboard.slot.tsx` looks up the sheet's descendants, works out each sheet's counts the same way as before, and adds them up.
- Whether a user counts as a steward is still decided on the sheet being viewed only.
- I moved the existing descendants lookup out of the consolidated panel into `features/consolidated/descendants.ts`, so the dashboard and that panel share it. The consolidated panel works as before.

**A separate bug I had to fix:** the first run passed 3 tests, but scenario 3 failed on something outside the dashboard. When the sheet was viewed as of an earlier date, a claim that was still open then showed the number it only got when it was settled later. Claims are now numbered when they settle, but the as-of view still showed the number for any claim opened by that date. In `RespondWithClaims.java`, the as-of view now shows a claim's number only if its status log has it settled by that date.

That fix changes as-of output beyond the dashboard, and I may have missed cases where a claim gets a number another way, such as being moved to another sheet. That's worth a look when you review it.
